summary: Pinnacles National Park lookout on North Chalone Peak, built 1952 after a 1951 blast and fire; the park has decided to demolish it, with funding unsecured.

facts.design: Octagonal 16 by 16 foot wood cab on a 20 foot steel tower enclosed in aluminum siding; revised CDF 809R design
facts.status_note: Standing, but Pinnacles National Park has decided to demolish it. A 2025 chapter report says demolition may come as late as 2031.
facts.location: Monterey County, California; North Chalone Peak, the high point of Pinnacles National Park

access.note: The summit is reached on foot. The cab door was boarded up at the May 2019 register visit, and public access to the inside is not established.

visit.trail_note: Summit hike from Bear Gulch Reservoir, about 9 miles round trip with roughly 2,040 feet of climbing (Parkwolf); the register describes 4.5 miles each way through a wilderness area.

events.note: Approval received for a $2,500 lookout station on North Chalone; sources read do not confirm the station was finished or whether it is the one destroyed in 1951
Two blasts and a fire wrecked the CCC-built lookout and a World War II aircraft warning building (reported July 1951)
Current tower built by the California Department of Forestry; replacement estimated at $17,000
Vandals broke into the lookout and lit a fire on the floor
Ownership transferred to the National Park Service
Registered January 12, 2002 as US 396, CA 47; nominated by Dave Doyle
May 7, 2019 register visit: door boarded up, windows broken, graffiti, wood siding and deck need replacing, Osborne fire finder still in place
Pinnacles National Park decided to demolish the tower; chapter report says demolition may be as late as 2031, funding not secured

notes_for_editor: Well sourced on history (newspaper run in the Forest Lookouts page, register visit report, 2025 chapter report, park guide). Points to check: (1) Demolition is reported second-hand by the FFLA California-South 2025 report from park correspondence dated 12/12/24; not confirmed with Pinnacles National Park. Worth a call before publishing the status note. (2) Elevation: the record's 949.8 m is the register's lookout figure (3,116 ft). Parkwolf and Wikidata give the summit of North Chalone Peak as 3,304 ft, so the two may describe different points; not reconciled, not used in the story. (3) Cost figures differ: 2018 stabilization $200,000 (register) and $300,000 to $1 million to restore (2025 report); the story says they may cover different work. (4) The 1935 station and the 1951 destroyed lookout are not confirmed as the same structure. (5) The 1951 cause differs between the 1951 report (butane from a refrigerator or stove) and the 1952 report (gas from a tank lit by a refrigerator pilot light); both are cited. Record kind enclosed_tower and height 6.1 m are consistent with the register's 20 ft steel tower. Access level closed reflects the boarded door and the unestablished public access, not a closure order. No new photos added. Budget: NHLR, Forest Lookouts page, Wikidata, Cal-South southern page, Parkwolf (moved page), plus the 2025 report; one search.
